newsitem.title: UK: Environmentalist calls for more UK bread wheat.
newsitem.headline: Environmentalist calls for more UK bread wheat.

text.p: Britain should increase production of milling and organic wheat, so as to cut the need to ship grain and reduce the pollution caused by long distance transport, a UK environmental group said on Tuesday.
"We grow much less bread wheat than we used to," Chris Emerson, of the SAFE alliance (Sustainable Agriculture, Food and the Environment) said.
"The situation where we export feed wheat and import milling wheat does seem strange," Emerson, who has written a new report on bread production in the UK, said.
"We are the sixth largest exporter of wheat in the world and yet we still import around 800,000 tonnes of bread-making wheat a year," Emerson, said in his report, called "Abusing our Loaf?"

Even if it all came from Europe, shipping this milling wheat would generate 11,250,000 kilogrammes of carbon dioxide, 45,000 kg of carbon monoxide and 150,000 kg of nitrous oxides, increasing air pollution and worsening the risk of global warming," the report said.
"As it is, some of the conventional wheat we import comes from as far away as Canada, making the pollution even worse."

Further pollution results from "the failure of the government to provide adequate incentives for organic agriculture in the UK, it said. It "resulted in the UK spending 500,000 stg on importing organic wheat half way around the world from Australia." Assuming these imports were shipped, they would have generated at least 31,200 kg of carbon monoxide, 1,248 kg of carbon monoxide and 4,160 kg of nitrogen oxides, "further adding to global pollution levels and countering the environmental benefits of organic production methods."
